name: Upstart
desc: AI lending marketplace that uses machine learning to approve personal, auto and home equity loans funded by partner banks.
markets: US consumers and partner banks and credit unions only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: US-only consumer lender; F1's growing US audience offers awareness, but the brand is B2B2C and domestic, a modest fit.

name: Flexera
desc: Software for IT asset management, software licence optimisation, cloud cost management and technology spend and risk intelligence for enterprises.
industry: IT asset and cloud cost management software
markets: Large enterprises and software producers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; Revenera division serves software vendors.
rationale: Global enterprise software vendor selling to CIOs; F1 B2B hospitality and data-driven cost themes could support enterprise sales.

name: Dunamu
desc: Operates Upbit, South Korea's largest cryptocurrency exchange, plus related blockchain and digital asset services for retail investors.
markets: Mainly South Korean retail crypto traders; Upbit-branded exchanges also operate in South-East Asian markets such as Indonesia and Thailand.
rationale: Rival crypto exchanges such as Crypto.com, OKX and Kraken sponsor F1; useful if Upbit grows outside Korea.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to merge with Naver Financial via share swap; completion not confirmed

name: DeepSeek
desc: Develops open-weight large language models and offers a chatbot app and paid API access to developers and businesses.
markets: Users and API customers worldwide, strongest in China; several countries restrict its app on data-privacy grounds.
rationale: Globally known AI brand, but low marketing culture and political and data-privacy sensitivities make an F1 deal unlikely.

name: Nexus Data Centers
desc: Data centre company described by Crunchbase as offering AI infrastructure; further products, customers and owners are not confirmed.
markets: Presumed US data centre operations only; no verified customers or international plans.
rationale: Little public information; B2B data-centre developers usually have limited brand marketing, so the F1 fit is unclear.

name: Prometheus
desc: AI start-up, also called Project Prometheus, applying artificial intelligence to engineering and manufacturing in the physical economy.
markets: Pre-revenue; no products or customers publicly confirmed and no verified international operations.
rationale: Pre-revenue AI lab co-led by Jeff Bezos; an engineering and manufacturing focus has a technology fit, but nothing to market yet.

name: Altius
desc: Telecom infrastructure company that owns mobile tower sites in India and leases them to telecom operators.
markets: Indian mobile network operators only; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B tower owner with few customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Atoms
desc: Robotics start-up that Crunchbase describes as developing industrial robotics; products and customers are not confirmed.
markets: No verified customers or international activity; details not confirmed.
rationale: Too little public information to judge; an early robotics start-up has limited budget and brand need for F1.

name: Digital Edge
desc: Builds and operates carrier-neutral data centres in Asia for cloud providers, internet companies and enterprises.
markets: Data centres across Asia-Pacific, including Japan, Korea, Indonesia, India and South-East Asia; Stonepeak-backed.
rationale: Asia-focused B2B infrastructure brand; Singapore and Japan races could host clients, but limited marketing culture.

name: DigitalOcean
desc: Cloud infrastructure provider offering virtual servers, managed databases, Kubernetes and GPU compute to developers, start-ups and small businesses.
markets: Customers in over 100 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, served from data centres on several continents.
rationale: Rivals AWS, Google and Oracle use F1 as a technology showcase; DigitalOcean could reach developers and small businesses globally.

name: Lenskart
desc: Designs, manufactures and sells prescription glasses, sunglasses and contact lenses online and through its own and franchised stores.
markets: Mainly India, plus stores in South-East Asia, Japan through Owndays, and the Middle East.
rationale: Consumer brand with heavy sports advertising and international growth; eyewear partners such as Ray-Ban and Oakley show the category fits F1.
changed: Listed on NSE and BSE in 2025

name: Lumen Technologies
desc: Provides fibre network, internet, security and cloud connectivity services to enterprises and public sector customers in the United States.
markets: Mainly US enterprise and government customers after selling its Latin American, EMEA and consumer fibre businesses.
rationale: Enterprise network provider with US focus and existing sports naming rights; US races could support B2B hospitality.
changed: Formerly CenturyLink; agreed in 2025 to sell its consumer fibre business to AT&T

name: MiniMax
desc: Develops multimodal AI models and consumer apps including Talkie, Xingye and the Hailuo AI video generation service.
markets: Consumer app users in China, North America, Europe and Asia; API customers for its models.
rationale: Consumer AI apps with global users and a new listing; F1 could build awareness outside China, though political sensitivities apply.
changed: Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January 2026

name: Public Storage
desc: Real estate investment trust that owns and operates self-storage facilities rented to households and businesses, plus tenant insurance.
markets: Self-storage facilities across the United States; holds a stake in Shurgard in Europe.
rationale: Domestic consumer real estate brand; F1 US races offer awareness, but limited strategic need.

name: Sabre Corporation
desc: Runs a global distribution system linking airlines, hotels and car rental firms with travel agencies, plus airline software.
markets: Airlines, hotels and travel agencies worldwide across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Travel technology B2B brand; F1's global travel circuit and airline partners could suit client hospitality.
changed: Sold its Hospitality Solutions business to TPG in 2025

name: Safe Superintelligence
desc: AI research company working on building safe superintelligence; it has released no products and has no customers.
markets: Pre-revenue; research offices in Palo Alto and Tel Aviv, with no commercial products.
rationale: Pre-revenue research lab with no product or customers to market; weak F1 fit despite its high profile.

name: SenseTime
desc: Develops computer vision, facial recognition, large language models and AI platforms for governments, enterprises and carmakers.
markets: Mainly mainland China and Hong Kong, with business in Asia and the Middle East; under US sanctions.
rationale: Subject to US government sanctions over surveillance concerns; restricted and unlikely F1 partner.

name: TP
desc: Outsourced customer experience provider running contact centres, digital support, content moderation and collections services for large companies.
markets: Operations in about 90 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B services firm whose large clients could be hosted at races; less consumer need for awareness.
changed: Rebranded from Teleperformance to TP

name: Verisk
desc: Provides data analytics, risk assessment software, catastrophe models and claims tools mainly to insurance companies.
markets: Mainly US insurers, with customers in Europe, Asia-Pacific and other international markets.
rationale: B2B analytics brand for insurers; data-analytics theme fits F1, but rivals are not sponsors and marketing is limited.

name: VIRTUS Data Centres
desc: Designs, builds and operates data centres in the UK and Europe for cloud providers and enterprises.
markets: Data centres in the UK, expanding into continental Europe including Germany.
rationale: B2B infrastructure brand; British Grand Prix hospitality could serve enterprise and cloud clients, but limited marketing need.

name: Waters
desc: Makes liquid chromatography, mass spectrometry and thermal analysis instruments, software and consumables for pharmaceutical and industrial laboratories.
markets: Laboratory customers worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, including China and India.
rationale: Global B2B instrument maker; precision-measurement theme exists, but little consumer marketing and no rivals in F1.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to combine with BD's Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business

name: Bending Spoons
desc: Acquires and operates digital products such as Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo and AOL, and builds apps such as Remini.
markets: Apps used by consumers and businesses worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Italian-founded owner of global consumer apps; F1 could support brand building for its portfolio, especially in Europe and the US.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq through an IPO in July 2026

name: Bitfarms
desc: Operates bitcoin mining data centres and is converting sites to high-performance computing and AI hosting.
markets: Mining operations in Canada and the United States; shifting toward HPC and AI data centre hosting.
rationale: Crypto miner with limited brand marketing; crypto sponsorship exists in F1, but miners rarely benefit.

name: Crusoe
desc: Builds and operates AI data centres and a GPU cloud that rents compute capacity to AI labs and enterprises.
industry: AI data centres and GPU cloud
markets: Mainly US campuses such as Abilene, Texas, plus data centre operations in Europe.
rationale: High-profile AI infrastructure firm; F1 technology partners such as CoreWeave show the category can use F1 for B2B profile.

name: Scale AI
desc: Provides data labelling, model evaluation and data infrastructure services used to train AI models for tech firms and governments.
markets: Mainly US AI labs, enterprises and the US government, with a contributor workforce in many countries.
rationale: B2B AI data provider; F1 hospitality could reach enterprise and government clients, but marketing need is moderate.
changed: Meta bought a 49% stake in 2025 and founder Alexandr Wang joined Meta

name: Aspen Technology
desc: Industrial software for process simulation, asset optimisation and operations used by energy, chemicals and engineering companies.
markets: Process-industry customers worldwide, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Industrial simulation software fits F1 engineering themes, but as an Emerson unit its marketing budget sits with its parent.
changed: Emerson acquired the remaining shares in 2025 and delisted it from Nasdaq

name: Telegram
desc: Cloud-based messaging app with chats, groups, channels, bots and mini apps, earning from premium subscriptions and advertising.
markets: Around one billion users worldwide, strong in Russia, Eastern Europe, India, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Massive global consumer audience overlaps with F1's fan base, but the company rarely sponsors and carries regulatory controversy.

name: UL Solutions
desc: Provides product safety testing, inspection, certification and software services to manufacturers and retailers.
markets: Manufacturers and retailers worldwide, with laboratories across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global B2B certification brand; safety and testing themes and B2B hospitality give a plausible fit.
changed: Listed on NYSE in 2024

name: Viasat
desc: Provides satellite broadband to homes, airlines, ships, enterprises and governments, plus defence and secure communications equipment.
markets: Customers worldwide through its own and Inmarsat satellites, with major aviation, maritime and government business.
rationale: Global connectivity provider for airlines and maritime; F1 could showcase technology, though defence work limits fit.
changed: Acquired Inmarsat in 2023

name: Digital Asset
desc: Develops the Daml smart contract language and Canton Network blockchain used by banks for tokenisation and settlement.
markets: Banks, asset managers and market infrastructure firms in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Institutional blockchain firm; finance and crypto sponsors are common in F1, but its buyers are few banks.

name: Kitopi
desc: Operates delivery-only cloud kitchens that prepare food for partner restaurant brands and its own brands sold through delivery apps.
markets: Gulf markets including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain.
rationale: Gulf consumer food business; Abu Dhabi, Saudi and Qatar races offer local reach, but brand awareness is limited.

name: Ripple
desc: Provides blockchain-based cross-border payments, custody services and the RLUSD stablecoin to banks, payment firms and enterprises.
markets: Financial institutions and enterprises across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Crypto and payments rivals such as Crypto.com, Coinbase and Circle sponsor F1; global institutional brand building fits.

name: Hyperliquid Strategies
desc: Digital asset treasury company that holds HYPE tokens of the Hyperliquid decentralised exchange on its balance sheet.
markets: No operating customers; a US-listed vehicle whose value depends on the HYPE token.
rationale: Token-holding vehicle with no operating brand to market; very weak F1 fit.
changed: Formed in 2025 through a merger with Sonnet BioTherapeutics

name: Avalon Labs
desc: Decentralised finance platform that Crunchbase says brings Bitcoin and other assets into lending and finance products.
markets: Headquarters, customers and markets are not confirmed; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Crypto sponsors are common in F1, but too little is confirmed about this platform to judge its fit.

name: Axiom Solutions International
desc: Company that Crunchbase says develops digital and electrical products and services; details are not confirmed.
markets: No verified customers, products, markets or international activity; expansion plans unknown.
rationale: Too little is known to judge the F1 fit; identity and business are unconfirmed.

name: CCC Intelligent Solutions
desc: Cloud software for auto insurance claims, repair estimating, parts and total-loss valuation used by insurers and repair shops.
markets: Mainly US insurers, repair shops, carmakers and parts suppliers; no verified major international expansion.
rationale: Automotive claims and repair software has a car-industry link, but customers are mostly domestic.
changed: Went public in 2021 via merger with Dragoneer Growth Opportunities Corp. II

name: Cyera
desc: Data security platform that discovers, classifies and protects sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises systems.
markets: Large enterprises mainly in the US, with R&D in Israel and customers in Europe.
rationale: Fast-growing cybersecurity firm; peers CrowdStrike, Zscaler and Okta use F1 for enterprise branding and hospitality.

name: Eurofiber
desc: Owns and operates fibre networks offering dark fibre, connectivity and data centre interconnect to businesses, telecoms and government.
markets: Netherlands, Belgium, France and Germany; customers are enterprises, operators and public bodies.
rationale: Regional B2B infrastructure owner; Dutch and Belgian races could host clients, but little brand marketing.

name: Figure AI
desc: Develops general-purpose humanoid robots and the Helix AI model for factory, logistics and eventual home use.
markets: Pre-revenue; pilot deployments in the US, including with BMW, and no verified international operations.
rationale: High-profile robotics brand with technology showcase appeal, but still pre-revenue with limited marketing budget.

name: Fireworks AI
desc: Inference platform that serves open-source and custom AI models to developers and enterprises through APIs and fine-tuning.
markets: Mainly US developers and enterprises via cloud API; no verified international operations.
rationale: Developer-focused AI infrastructure; F1 tech partners like Groq show the category, but budget and brand need are early.

name: Flexential
desc: Provides colocation, managed hosting, cloud, connectivity and disaster recovery services from data centres across the United States.
markets: Mid-size and large enterprises in the United States only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Domestic B2B infrastructure provider; US races offer client hospitality but limited marketing need.
changed: Formed in 2018 from the merger of Peak 10 and ViaWest

name: Joulent
desc: Company that Crunchbase says develops large-scale energy systems; products, customers and owners are not confirmed.
markets: No verified customers, markets or international activity; expansion plans unknown.
rationale: Too little is known to judge; energy infrastructure developers rarely market to consumers.

name: Motive
desc: Fleet management platform offering AI dashcams, electronic logging devices, telematics and spend management to trucking and field fleets.
markets: Fleets in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
rationale: Vehicle and driver safety technology links to motorsport; US races could support brand building with fleet operators.
changed: Renamed Motive from KeepTruckin in 2022

name: Pinterest
desc: Visual discovery platform where users save ideas for shopping, recipes, home and fashion, earning revenue from advertising.
markets: Users and advertisers across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Consumer platform growing outside the US; F1's young and female audience growth aligns with its users and advertisers.

name: Reflection AI
desc: AI lab developing open foundation models and software agents for AI-assisted software development.
markets: Early commercial stage; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Well-funded AI lab; peers Anthropic and Cohere partner with F1 teams, but it has little to market yet.

name: Skild AI
desc: Develops Skild Brain, a general-purpose AI model to control many types of robots.
markets: Early stage; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Robotics AI with technology appeal, but early stage with limited brand need; a weak F1 fit for now.

name: Thinking Machines Lab
desc: AI research and product company offering the Tinker fine-tuning service and developing open-weight language models.
markets: Early commercial stage selling to developers and researchers; no verified international operations.
rationale: Prominent AI lab; F1 AI partners show category fit, but its products are early and developer-focused.

name: ClickUp
desc: Cloud work management software combining tasks, docs, chat, whiteboards and AI tools for teams.
markets: Teams worldwide, mainly North America and Europe; no verified local operations beyond those.
rationale: Peers Atlassian and Smartsheet sponsor F1; ClickUp could use F1 for B2B brand awareness.

name: MKS Inc.
desc: Supplies instruments, subsystems, lasers, photonics and specialty chemicals used in semiconductor, circuit board and industrial manufacturing.
markets: Semiconductor and electronics manufacturers in North America, Asia and Europe.
rationale: B2B supplier with precision engineering ties; F1 could support hospitality with Asian chipmakers, but marketing need is low.
changed: Renamed MKS Inc. from MKS Instruments

name: Dayforce
desc: Cloud human capital management software for payroll, HR, workforce management, benefits and talent for employers.
markets: Employers mainly in North America, plus the UK, Europe and Australia.
rationale: HR software peers UKG, Workday and Businessolver sponsor F1; B2B brand building fits.
changed: Formerly Ceridian; agreed in 2025 to be taken private by Thoma Bravo

name: Clio
desc: Cloud legal practice management software for law firms covering case management, billing, client intake and AI tools.
markets: Law firms in North America, the UK, Europe and Australia; expanding legal research through vLex.
rationale: Professional-services software; F1 hospitality could reach law firm leaders, but niche audience limits fit.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to acquire vLex

name: Quantum Computing Inc.
desc: Develops photonic quantum technologies and thin-film lithium niobate chips for sensing, computing and security applications.
markets: Small revenue from US research and government customers; no verified international operations.
rationale: Speculative early-stage quantum technology firm with tiny revenue and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Rippling
desc: Workforce management software combining HR, payroll, benefits, IT device management and spend in one system.
markets: Businesses mainly in the US, expanding in the UK, Europe, Canada and other international markets.
rationale: HR software peers sponsor F1; Rippling's international expansion and marketing culture support B2B brand building.

name: TierPoint
desc: Provides colocation, managed hosting, cloud, disaster recovery and security services from data centres across the United States.
markets: Mid-market enterprises in the United States only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Domestic B2B data centre provider with limited marketing culture and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Paxos
desc: Regulated blockchain company issuing stablecoins and offering tokenisation, crypto brokerage and custody to financial firms.
markets: Enterprise financial clients mainly in the US, with regulated operations in Singapore, Abu Dhabi and Europe.
rationale: Stablecoin rivals such as Circle partner with F1; B2B brand building with fintech clients is plausible.

name: Nothing
desc: Designs and sells smartphones, earbuds, headphones and wearables under the Nothing and CMF brands.
markets: Sold in Europe, India, the US, Japan and other Asian markets directly and through retailers.
rationale: Design-led consumer tech brand targeting young buyers in Europe, India and the US; F1's audience matches well.

name: SK Horizon
desc: Company that Crunchbase describes as an AI data centre infrastructure business; ownership and operations are not confirmed.
markets: Presumed South Korean operations; no verified customers or expansion plans.
rationale: Too little is confirmed to judge; B2B data-centre infrastructure normally has limited marketing need.

name: Wistron Corporation
desc: Designs and manufactures notebooks, servers, networking and medical equipment for global electronics brands as a contract manufacturer.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia; factories in Taiwan, China, Mexico and South-East Asia.
rationale: B2B contract manufacturer; customers Dell, HP and Lenovo sponsor F1, but Wistron has little brand need.
changed: Spun off from Acer in 2000

name: Flex
desc: Contract manufacturer designing and building products for automotive, healthcare, industrial, communications and data centre customers.
markets: Manufacturing in over 30 countries serving customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global manufacturer with automotive and data-centre customers; F1 hospitality could support B2B relationships.
changed: Formerly Flextronics

name: Bird
desc: Cloud communications platform offering SMS, voice, WhatsApp and email messaging APIs plus customer engagement software for businesses.
markets: Businesses worldwide across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Peer Infobip partners with F1; Bird could use F1 for B2B brand building with marketers.
changed: Renamed Bird from MessageBird in 2024

name: D-Wave Quantum
desc: Builds annealing and gate-model quantum computers offered through its Leap cloud service and on-premise systems to enterprises and researchers.
markets: Customers and partners in North America, Europe and Japan; operations in the US and Canada.
rationale: Quantum technology could be a showcase, but revenue is small and marketing budgets limited.
changed: Went public in 2022 via SPAC merger

name: Flapping Airplanes
desc: Artificial intelligence research start-up; its products, customers and backers are not confirmed.
markets: Pre-revenue research company; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Research-stage AI lab with no product or customers to market yet; weak F1 fit.

name: Guidewire Software
desc: Provides policy, billing and claims software plus cloud and analytics services for property and casualty insurers.
markets: Insurance carriers in over 40 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global B2B software with insurer clients; F1 hospitality could support enterprise sales, but niche audience.

name: Keyfactor
desc: Provides public key infrastructure, certificate lifecycle management and code signing software for enterprise machine identity security.
markets: Enterprises in North America and Europe across finance, healthcare and manufacturing.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers such as CrowdStrike and Zscaler sponsor F1; plausible B2B brand building.

name: Kpler
desc: Provides real-time data and analytics on commodity flows, shipping and energy markets using vessel and satellite tracking.
markets: Traders, banks, energy firms and governments across Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Data analytics brand serving energy and shipping traders; F1 hospitality can reach Gulf and Asian clients.
changed: Acquired MarineTraffic in 2023 and Spire Maritime in 2025

name: Megaport
desc: Provides software-defined network services that connect enterprises to cloud providers and data centres on demand.
markets: Enterprises and service providers across Asia-Pacific, North America and Europe.
rationale: Global connectivity brand; F1 technology partnerships could raise awareness with enterprise IT buyers.

name: Neuralink
desc: Develops implantable brain-computer interfaces to help people with paralysis control devices and communicate.
markets: Pre-revenue; clinical trials in the US, Canada, the UK and the United Arab Emirates.
rationale: Pre-revenue medical device developer; Musk's profile gives awareness, but it has no product to market.

name: Oklo
desc: Develops small advanced fission power plants and fuel recycling to supply electricity to data centres and industry.
markets: Pre-revenue; project sites in the United States, including Idaho, and US data centre customers.
rationale: Pre-revenue nuclear developer; clean-power messaging could suit F1 sustainability themes, but nothing to sell yet.
changed: Went public in 2024 via SPAC merger with AltC Acquisition Corp

name: Persistent Systems
desc: Provides software engineering, digital transformation, cloud, data and AI services to banking, healthcare and technology clients.
markets: Clients mainly in North America, plus Europe, India and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: IT services peers Cognizant, Mphasis and Globant use F1 for client hospitality; a strong fit.

name: Quantinuum
desc: Builds trapped-ion quantum computers and quantum software for enterprises, governments and researchers.
markets: Customers in the US, UK, Europe and Japan; operations in the US and UK.
rationale: Quantum technology showcase potential; as a Honeywell subsidiary with B2B focus, marketing need is moderate.
changed: Formed in 2021 by merging Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum

name: SandboxAQ
desc: Develops AI and quantum-based software for drug and materials discovery, cybersecurity and navigation for enterprises and governments.
markets: Enterprise and government customers mainly in the US; no verified international operations.
rationale: B2B deep-tech firm selling to enterprises and governments; an F1 technology partnership is plausible but not obvious.
changed: Spun out of Alphabet in 2022

name: Supabase
desc: Open-source backend platform offering a Postgres database, authentication, storage and real-time APIs to application developers.
markets: Developers and start-ups in many countries, with a distributed team; no other verified international operations.
rationale: Developer platform; peers Vercel and Confluent partner with F1, giving a plausible B2B awareness case.

name: ClickHouse
desc: Offers the open-source ClickHouse column-oriented analytics database and a managed cloud service for real-time analytics.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia; subsidiary in Amsterdam.
rationale: Data infrastructure peers such as Confluent and NetApp partner with F1; plausible tech showcase.
changed: Spun out of Yandex in 2021

name: Advanced Machine Intelligence
desc: AI research start-up co-founded by Yann LeCun developing world models and advanced machine intelligence.
markets: Pre-revenue research company; no commercial products or verified international operations.
rationale: Research-stage lab with no product to market yet; LeCun's profile aside, a weak F1 fit.

name: Apptronik
desc: Designs and builds general-purpose humanoid robots, notably Apollo, for logistics and manufacturing work.
markets: Pre-revenue; pilot projects with partners such as Mercedes-Benz and GXO.
rationale: Its pilot with Mercedes-Benz gives a motorsport link, but the company is pre-revenue with limited budget.

name: Bedrock Robotics
desc: Develops sensor, computing and machine-learning systems that automate heavy construction equipment, beginning with excavators.
markets: Early stage, serving US construction contractors; no verified international operations.
rationale: Early-stage B2B construction technology company with limited brand need and budget; weak F1 fit.

name: CAIS
desc: Platform giving independent financial advisers access to alternative investments such as hedge funds, private equity and real estate.
markets: Financial advisers in the United States; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Wealth platform with US advisers; hospitality at US races is plausible but not obvious.

name: Claroty
desc: Cybersecurity software that protects industrial, healthcare and building systems connected to operational technology networks.
markets: Industrial, healthcare and utility customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers such as CrowdStrike sponsor F1; industrial and manufacturing clients suit B2B hospitality.

name: Grafana Labs
desc: Sells Grafana Cloud and open-source tools for monitoring metrics, logs and traces in software systems.
markets: Customers and staff across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Observability peers Dynatrace and Splunk sponsor F1; telemetry fits racing data themes.

name: Ineffable Intelligence
desc: AI start-up building machine learning systems that learn from experience, reportedly founded by David Silver.
markets: Pre-revenue research company; no commercial products or verified international operations.
rationale: Research-stage lab with no product to market yet and little brand need; weak F1 fit.

name: Nexthink
desc: Digital employee experience software that monitors devices and applications so IT teams can find and fix problems.
markets: Large enterprises across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Swiss-founded enterprise software; F1 B2B hospitality fits IT buyers, as peers like TeamViewer show.

name: Physical Intelligence
desc: Develops AI foundation models for general-purpose robot control, including the pi0 and pi0.5 models.
markets: Research stage; no verified customers or international operations.
rationale: Research-stage robotics AI firm with no product to market yet; weak F1 fit.

name: V.tal
desc: Neutral wholesale fibre network company selling connectivity, backhaul and network services to telecom operators in Brazil.
markets: Telecom operators and businesses in Brazil only; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Domestic B2B infrastructure; the Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers hospitality, but marketing need is low.
changed: Created in 2021 from Oi's fibre network with BTG Pactual funds

name: Waabi
desc: Develops autonomous trucking software, the Waabi Driver, trained with a generative AI simulator.
markets: Pre-commercial operations in Canada and the US, including Texas, with partners Volvo and Uber Freight.
rationale: Autonomy technology fits motorsport themes, but it is pre-revenue with limited marketing need.

name: Xanadu
desc: Builds photonic quantum computers and the PennyLane open-source quantum software library for researchers and enterprises.
markets: Research, enterprise and government users mainly in Canada and abroad via cloud; little verified revenue.
rationale: Deep-tech showcase potential, but early stage with limited budget; weak to moderate F1 fit.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to go public via SPAC merger with Crane Harbor Acquisition Corp

name: Tekion
desc: Cloud software for car dealerships covering dealer management, CRM, finance and service tools for dealers and automakers.
markets: Car dealers and automakers in the United States and Canada; development team in India.
rationale: Automotive retail software; F1 hospitality could reach carmaker and dealer group clients.

name: Zebra Technologies
desc: Makes barcode scanners, printers, RFID readers, mobile computers and machine vision for retail, logistics, healthcare and manufacturing.
markets: Customers in over 100 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Sports tracking experience with the NFL and logistics clients make an F1 technology partnership plausible.

name: Dataminr
desc: Uses AI to scan public data such as social media and news and alerts companies and governments to emerging risks.
markets: Corporate, media and public-sector clients in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Real-time data brand; B2B hospitality with corporate security buyers is plausible but not obvious.

name: Figma
desc: Browser-based collaborative interface design and prototyping software, with FigJam whiteboards and Dev Mode for product teams.
markets: Designers and developers worldwide across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rival Adobe partners with F1; Figma could use F1 for brand and design-led campaigns.
changed: Listed on NYSE in 2025 after Adobe's acquisition was abandoned in 2023

name: KoBold Metals
desc: Uses AI and geoscience data to explore for battery minerals such as copper, nickel, cobalt and lithium.
markets: Pre-revenue; exploration projects in Zambia, Canada, Australia and the US.
rationale: Pre-revenue explorer with no consumer brand; battery-mineral narrative is a weak F1 fit.
